guard_streams.source: National Rolling Open Market Review May 2026 Request For Information
guard_streams.write_limit: The RFI defines evidence, classification and procurement rules. Supplier submissions and subsidy eligibility are not equivalent to live orderability or measured fixed-broadband performance at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: The RFI cites £5 billion for the hardest-to-reach parts of the UK.
BDUK describes a procurement approach for gigabit-capable wholesale infrastructure.
Potential intervention areas focus on places with no current infrastructure or planned build within three years.
Voucher projects before issue are treated as White in the stated data assessment.
Issued vouchers are classified Under Review in the stated treatment.
Claimed vouchers are treated as Grey because they should be gigabit-connected.
The RFI lists GBVS, Superfast, GIS, LFFN, RGC, GigaHubs and local-body projects as intervention data.
BDUK intends to procure solutions capable of at least 1 Gbps download.
Suppliers may submit firm and credible plans showing that public subsidy is not warranted.
Final intervention areas may be a subset of premises classified White.

guard_streams.source: National Rolling Open Market Review January 2026 Request For Information
guard_streams.write_limit: The January RFI is a supplier-evidence and subsidy-targeting specification. Its classification logic and investment plans require later evaluation and cannot independently verify current selected-parcel service.

facts.detail: The January RFI cites £5 billion for the hardest-to-reach parts of the UK.
The procurement approach is described as a successor to the Superfast broadband Programme.
BDUK states it seeks industry collaboration to maximise efficiency and minimise market distortion.
Potential intervention areas are places without infrastructure or planned build within three years.
Projects before voucher issue are treated as White.
Issued vouchers are treated as Under Review.
Claimed vouchers are treated as Grey.
The intended procured solutions must be capable of at least 1 Gbps download.
Suppliers may provide firm and credible investment plans during NR OMR and Public Review.
Final intervention areas may be a White subset after overlays for active and planned interventions.
